segments.he: גְּמָ׳ הָעוּבָּר. אִי בַּת כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא — פָּסֵיל לָהּ. ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ — פְּרָט לִמְעוּבֶּרֶת. אִי בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן הִיא — לֹא מַאֲכִיל לָהּ, יָלוּד — מַאֲכִיל, שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָלוּד — אֵינוֹ מַאֲכִיל.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» It is taught in the mishna that «the fetus» disqualifies its mother from partaking of teruma and does not enable her to do so. The Gemara explains: «If she is the daughter of a priest» married «to an Israelite,» and her husband died and left her pregnant, the fetus «disqualifies her» from partaking of teruma, as it is stated: “But if a priest’s daughter be a widow, or divorced, and have no child, and is returned to her father’s house, as in her youth, she may eat of her father’s bread” (Leviticus 22:13). The phrase «“as in her youth” excludes a pregnant woman,» whose body has changed from her youth. «If» she «is an Israelite woman» married «to a priest,» the fetus «does not enable her to partake,» as «one who was born enables» others «to partake» of teruma, whereas «one who is not» yet «born does not enable» others «to partake.»
